paragraphs: I've spent a long time working in Lafayette and the surrounding hills, and homes along Reliez Valley Road and its quiet courts always get my attention  -  especially when they sit on nearly three-quarters of an acre with unobstructed views of Mount Diablo. When 15 Surmont Ct came to market, I noticed it right away: the lot position, the wrap-around deck, the pool and sports court, and those open wood beam ceilings on the main level tell a compelling story about how this home actually lives. When the listing came off the market after 62 days without a sale, I thought it was worth reaching out.

Sixty-two days is long enough for a pattern to form in buyers' minds, and the pattern here wasn't about the home  -  it was about how the home was presented. A property with this much going for it, at $514 per square foot, sits well below what Lafayette buyers typically pay for something with a lot like this and a floor plan this flexible. That gap between the underlying value and the outcome usually points to a strategy problem: the right buyers weren't found, or the story that would have motivated them to schedule a showing was never clearly told.

I've put together a short analysis of what the listing history suggests and how I'd approach a relaunch differently. It's specific to 15 Surmont Ct  -  the views, the multi-level layout, the in-law suite, the outdoor amenities  -  not a generic overview of the Lafayette market. I think you'll find it useful whether you decide to work with me or not.

If you're already working with a real estate agent toward a new listing, please feel free to set this aside  -  no pressure at all. But if you're still weighing your options, I'd welcome a conversation.

cover.tagline: The Blueprint for a Successful Sale

exec_summary.headline: A Multi-Level Reliez Valley Estate with Panoramic Views  -  and a Listing That Didn't Show It
exec_summary.p1: 15 Surmont Ct has the kind of physical profile that Lamorinda buyers search for and rarely find: a true 0.73-acre lot at the end of a private court, sweeping views of Mount Diablo, a flexible 3,498 square foot floor plan with a self-contained lower-level suite, and outdoor amenities  -  pool, sundeck, sports court, firepit  -  that would cost well over six figures to replicate. The open beam ceiling living room, wrap-around deck, and three fireplaces give the home a character that photographs well when shot correctly. This is a property that should have attracted serious buyer interest quickly.
exec_summary.p2: The listing history tells a different story. After 62 days on the market, the home came off without a sale. At $514 per square foot, it was priced well below the Lafayette benchmark for a home of this quality and lot size  -  so the issue wasn't an aggressive number. The issue was that the strategy never made a clear case for what the home offered at that price. The Mount Diablo views, the court location, the multi-generational layout, and the outdoor living package were all mentioned, but they weren't staged as the headline. Buyers comparing options need a reason to drive out to Surmont Ct. A description that buries the view and the lot in a list of features isn't that reason.
exec_summary.p3: A relaunch needs to do one thing above all else: put the view, the lot, and the lifestyle front and center  -  visually and in every word of the listing  -  so that the buyers who would pay a premium for exactly this kind of property find it before they settle for something else.

forensics.title: Friction #1: 62 Days Created a Story the Home Didn't Deserve
forensics.body: Once a listing crosses the 45-day mark, buyer psychology shifts in a specific and predictable way. Buyers stop asking 'Is this a good home?' and start asking 'What's wrong with it?' At 62 days, that skepticism was fully in place for 15 Surmont Ct  -  and it had nothing to do with the home itself. A 0.73-acre lot with Mount Diablo views and a pool, priced at $514 per square foot, is not a hard sell. It's a distribution and timing problem: the buyers who would have moved quickly on this home were never reached in a concentrated enough window to generate the momentum a property like this needed. More time on the same strategy doesn't fix that. A fresh start with a different approach does.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork uses geo-targeted digital campaigns to reach SF and East Bay buyers who are actively researching Lamorinda before they've committed to a neighborhood  -  putting 15 Surmont Ct in front of decision-makers while they're still forming their shortlist, not after they've already scheduled showings elsewhere.

forensics.title: Friction #2: The Visual Story of This Home Was Never Told
forensics.body: The open beam ceilings, the wrap-around deck overlooking Mount Diablo, the pool and sports court, and the court-end privacy are exactly the kind of assets that sell Lafayette homes at the top of the price range. But assets like these live or die on photography and media. Standard MLS angles  -  a wide shot of the living room, a flat exterior from the driveway  -  leave the panoramic view invisible and the setting unexplained. At $1,798,000, buyers comparing this home to others in Lafayette needed to feel the lot, the view, and the outdoor package before they ever scheduled a showing. Without the right visual, a home like this reads as spacious but unremarkable. The character that justifies the number stayed hidden.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork's Sky Tour puts the lot, the court position, the view corridor toward Mount Diablo, and the outdoor amenities in context that no ground photograph can replicate  -  giving online buyers the full picture before they decide whether to make the drive.

forensics.title: Friction #3: The Listing Description Enumerated Features Instead of Building a Case
forensics.body: The listing description for 15 Surmont Ct ran through a long list of features  -  Dacor range, Arlo cameras, Nest thermostat, Shoji screens  -  but never assembled them into a coherent story about why this home is worth $1,798,000 and what kind of life it makes possible. Buyers in this price range are comparison shoppers. They read listings carefully, and they respond to narrative clarity, not inventory lists. The view of Mount Diablo from the wrap-around deck is mentioned mid-paragraph. The lower-level in-law suite is framed as a footnote. The 0.73-acre lot and court privacy barely register. A buyer skimming that description doesn't come away with a clear picture of what makes 15 Surmont Ct different from every other five-bedroom in Lafayette. They move on.
forensics.brightwork_contrast: BrightWork's Zillow Showcase placement pairs a purpose-built narrative  -  written the way a great buyer's agent describes a home to a motivated client  -  with premium portal visibility that routes all buyer inquiries directly back to the listing team, not to a random third-party agent.

positioning_table.verdict: At $514/sqft versus a benchmark range of $650-$920/sqft, this home sits near the lower end of that range. At $514 per square foot, 15 Surmont Ct came to market at the low end of the Lafayette fixer range  -  a notable discount given the lot size, the view, the outdoor amenities, and the multi-level floor plan. The number was not the obstacle. The gap between what this home actually offers and what the marketing communicated is what held buyers back. A relaunch built around the view, the lot, and the lifestyle should close that gap quickly.

pillars.title: Pillar I  -  Lead with the View, the Lot, and the Court Position
pillars.body: The single most important thing a relaunch of 15 Surmont Ct needs to do is make the Mount Diablo view and the 0.73-acre court setting the headline  -  not a supporting detail. Buyers who are willing to pay a premium for privacy, outdoor space, and a setting they can't find closer to downtown Lafayette need to understand immediately that this home has all three. That means purpose-built narrative, photography that captures the view from the deck, and a Sky Tour that shows the lot and the surrounding hillside in a way no ground photograph can.

pillars.title: Pillar II  -  Tell the In-Law Suite Story to the Right Buyers
pillars.body: The lower-level suite  -  bedroom, full bath, separate living areas  -  is a meaningful differentiator for a specific and growing segment of Lafayette buyers: multi-generational households, families with college-age children returning home, and buyers who want a dedicated home office or guest setup with real separation from the main living areas. That's a story worth telling directly and specifically, not burying at the end of a long listing description. A 3D Matterport tour lets those buyers walk the lower level from anywhere and understand exactly how it functions before they ever schedule a showing.

pillars.title: Pillar III  -  Reintroduce the Home with a Clean Start
pillars.body: After 62 days on the market, the stigma that accumulates around a stale listing is real  -  and it doesn't go away on its own. A relaunch of 15 Surmont Ct needs a full media rebuild: new photography, new narrative, and a distribution strategy that reaches buyers who were never exposed to the original listing. BrightWork's off-market private buyer list at offmarket.brightworkrealty.com gives us a way to reintroduce the home quietly to vetted, motivated buyers before it goes live again  -  so the public launch starts with momentum instead of from zero.
